- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing near-term price momentum.
- After sharp spikes in true prices (e.g., 71.17, 72.65, 73.14), forecasts overshoot initially but then correct — indicating model overreacts to volatility.
- Model shows weak mean reversion: fails to pull prices back toward historical averages after peaks.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the middle of the horizon, underestimating the upward trend that emerges later.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the first 10–15 days, then gradually improves — suggesting a calibration lag or delayed response to new data.
- Forecasts often underestimate the magnitude of true price increases, especially in the last 5–10 days of the 30-day window.
